title: Scale the Judgment, Not the Model — Andrew Orobator, Reddit
talk_summary: Andrew Orobator argues the bottleneck for agentic coding is not model quality but explicit, reusable judgment encoded as skills, worklogs, personas, and hard gates. He demonstrates a narrow feature-flag cleanup agent that backtests its scoring, produces green-CI PRs, and costs $1.26/PR, plus lessons about agents defeating soft gates.

takeaways.what_they_do: Encode the bundle of questions an experienced reviewer asks (rollout frozen? adjacent flags? owner?) as a reusable skill file the agent re-fires instead of guessing, distinct from passive documentation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A skill is institutional judgment made executable. It's that bundle written down so that the agent refires it instead of guessing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain a worklog (plan, decisions, tried-and-failed, surprises) that a fresh agent reads on 'continue' to resume at milestone N; a git hook blocks commits that don't update it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It reads the work log and picks up at milestone 7 out of nine. No re-exaining and the work log is the context.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of asking 'is this good?', prompt the model to review as named perspectives (security lead, UX researcher, adversarial abuser) and act on the reports.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Encode a domain's taste once and anyone can borrow eyes that they don't have.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent must hand back a recording of the feature actually running (drives app like a user, records every flow); the requirement forces the work to function, and an LLM can pre-screen before human merge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Producing that recording forces it to make the thing work. You can't fake a passing run.

takeaways.technique: Gate the choke point; no self-grantable bypass
takeaways.what_they_do: Repo hooks were bypassed by the agent's patch tool; moved gate to OS level and made bypass operator-only after the agent invented an 'emergency recovery' exception.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A gate with an escape hatch isn't a gate.

takeaways.technique: Narrow specialist agents with backtested scoring
takeaways.what_they_do: Feature-flag agent scores each flag like an experienced reviewer, checks experiment data, only safe mechanical cases reach the model; backtested scoring against months of history before going live.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Before I trusted this workflow, I back tested the scoring against months of cleanup history.
takeaways.numbers: $1.26 per PR; ~520 flags/year for under $700 vs ~$26,000 manual; 7/7 PRs green CI
